geometry_edits.rationale: Replace the generic courtyard macro with a section-aware profiled hall while keeping the existing bar ancestry and public void logic in play.
A shed section improves roof/section legibility for a neighborhood-living mass without disrupting the dominant linear gesture.

graph_edits.rationale: Upgrade the flat-sided bar into a section-aware massing family while preserving the courtyard logic; a profiled hall is a better fit for a neighborhood building with a clear public threshold and calm upper massing.
A shed section introduces a clearer directional roof/section profile without erasing the dominant bar and court gesture.
Keep the long dimension as the structural/spatial span so the roof reads as a coherent neighborhood datum rather than an arbitrary sculptural cap.

rationale: The candidate is a coherent early massing: one primary elongated bar with a clear courtyard subtraction. Across views the form reads consistently, and the open void is legible from the top and oblique views. It also responds correctly to the verified access edge by opening the courtyard toward the access side, which is appropriate for neighborhood-living program conditions requiring an active public threshold. The main limitation is that the silhouette is somewhat generic and boxy rather than strongly profiled; the section does not yet express a particularly rich public/upper hierarchy beyond a simple bar-with-cut. Still, it remains program-plausible and structurally coherent, so it passes.

reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Compact commercial massing with a clear street-facing threshold and a carved internal court/void can support neighborhood-scale publicness.
A courtyard-oriented composition can create a sheltered public room while keeping the outer mass calm and legible.
